title: Working From Home: Finding Balance
summary: Ama and Carlos compare the freedom and the hidden problems of remote work.

cover.scene: Flat 2D illustration: Ama and Carlos sitting on a sofa with laptops and mugs, a plant and a bright window behind them, no text

sentences.text: Carlos, you have been working from home for a year now. Do you still enjoy it?
Mostly, yes. I save two hours a day because I do not have to commute.
That is a huge advantage. I would use that time to exercise or cook properly.
In theory, yes. In practice, I often start working earlier and finish much later.
Really? I thought flexibility was the main benefit of remote work.
It is, but the boundary between my job and my private life has become blurred.
I understand. When your laptop is always on the kitchen table, it is hard to switch off.
Exactly. Last week I answered an email at ten at night, and I felt ridiculous.
Did anyone expect you to reply at that hour?
Not at all. It was my own habit. Nobody had asked me to do it.
Then maybe you should set stricter rules for yourself.
You are right. I am thinking of creating a small routine to mark the end of the day.

quiz.q: What is one benefit Carlos mentions?
quiz.explain: He saves two hours a day because he does not commute.

options: Work and private life are mixed together.
quiz.explain: He says the boundary between job and private life is blurred.

quiz.q: Who asked Carlos to reply at ten at night?
quiz.explain: It was his own habit; nobody asked him.

sentences.text: So what kind of routine do you have in mind?
First, I want to go for a short walk before I open my laptop, as if I were going to the office.
That is clever. It helps your brain to switch into work mode.
Then I plan to take a proper lunch break away from the screen.
I find that very difficult. I often eat while I am answering messages.
Which is not good for concentration, as far as I know.
True. Last month I made a mistake in a report because I was distracted.
At the end of the day, I will close the laptop and put it in a drawer.
Out of sight, out of mind. I might copy that idea.
It also helps to talk to colleagues, because remote work can feel lonely.
Definitely. I schedule a video call with a friend every Friday just to chat.
That is a lovely way to end the week. Maybe I should join you next time.

quiz.q: Why does Carlos want to walk before work?
options: To prepare his mind for work
quiz.explain: It helps his brain switch into work mode.

quiz.explain: She made a mistake in a report because she was distracted.
